The Qur'an verse (surah 89, verse 1 is "By the dawn"):

﴿By the dawn﴾ i.e., the dawn of every day.
﴿And by ten nights﴾ i.e., the ten (days) of Dhu al-Hijjah.
"And by the even" (al-shaf') — the pair, "and the odd" (al-watr), where the waw may be pronounced with a fatha or a kasra, both being dialectal forms: the single, unpaired.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 89, verse 6:

﴿Have you not seen﴾ know, O Muhammad, ﴿how your Lord dealt with ʿĀd﴾

Iram is the first ʿAd, so "Iram" is either an explanatory apposition (ʿatf bayan) or a substitute (badal) for it, and it is not declined (lā yanṣarif) because of its being a proper name (ʿalamiyya) and its feminine form (taʾnith). "Dhāt al-ʿimād" means of the tall pillars, i.e., their height: the height of the tallest of them was four hundred cubits (dhirāʿ).

Qur'anic quotation: ﴿Iram, [the people of] the pillared [city]﴾
﴿Whose like had not been created in the lands﴾ in their might and their strength.
﴿And Thamud, who hewed﴾ cut out ﴿the rocks﴾, the plural of ṣakhrah (rock), and took them as dwellings ﴿in the valley﴾, the Wadi al-Qura.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 89, verse 16:

﴿But as for man, when his Lord tests him and so restricts his provision, he says, "My Lord has humiliated me."﴾ He restricts his provision for him, so he says, "My Lord has humiliated me."

﷽ — no, I'll translate the passage directly.

﴿Nay [kallā]﴾ is a rebuke (radʿ), meaning: honour does not lie in wealth, nor humiliation in poverty; rather, it lies in obedience and disobedience. The Meccan unbelievers do not pay heed to this. ﴿Nay, you do not honour the orphan﴾: they do not treat him kindly despite their wealth, or they do not give him his right of inheritance.
"And you do not urge one another" (ولا تحاضون) — themselves or others — "to feed the poor" (على طعام) — i.e., to give food to (إطعام) — "the needy" (المسكين).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 89, verse 19:

﴿And you devour the heritage﴾ (al-turath), meaning the inheritance, ﴿with greedy devouring﴾ (aklan lamman), i.e., intense, because of their combining (lamminhim) the share of the women and the children of the inheritance with their own share of it, or with their own wealth.
﴿And you love wealth with an intense love﴾, i.e., a great deal, so they do not spend it. And in one reading, with the upper (taa') letter in the four verbs.
"No!" is a rebuke to them concerning that. ﴿When the earth is pounded, pounded﴾ — it is shaken until every building upon it collapses and is annihilated.

"And your Lord has come, and the angels, rank upon rank."

Tafsir al-Jalalayn: ﴿And your Lord has come﴾, i.e., His command (amr), ﴿and the angels﴾, i.e., the angels (al-malaikah), ﴿rank upon rank﴾ — a circumstantial clause (hal), meaning arrayed in rows, or possessing many rows.

And Hell is brought forth on that Day. It is led by seventy thousand bridles, each bridle held by seventy thousand angels, and it has a roaring and a raging. ﴿On that Day﴾ is a substitute (badal) for "when" (idha) and its response (jawab). ﴿Man will remember﴾, that is, the disbeliever, what he neglected (farrata) therein. ﴿But how will the remembrance benefit him?﴾ This is an interrogative used in the sense of negation; that is, his remembrance will not benefit him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 89, verse 24:

﴿He will say﴾ while remembering it, ﴿"Would that I had sent forward﴾ [good deeds] ﴿for my life﴾ [of the Hereafter, which is the good life], or for the time of my life in this world"], meaning good works and faith.

"So on that Day none will punish as He punishes" — read with a kasra on the dhal (يُعَذِّبُ, i.e. yu'adhdhibu with the dhal pronounced in the kasra form), "His punishment" — that is, Allah's — "anyone" — that is, He does not entrust it to another.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 89, verse 26:

﴿And none binds as He binds.﴾ Likewise, "لا يُوثِق" (lā yūthiq) with a kasra on the thāʾ. In another qirāʾa (recitation), with a fatḥa on the dhāl and the thāʾ, the pronoun in ʿadhābihi (His punishment) and waththāqihi (His binding) refers to the disbeliever. The meaning: no one is punished like His punishment, and no one is bound like His binding.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 89, verse 27:

﴿O soul at peace!﴾ — the secure one, and it is the believing soul.
